channel.title: WSJ | World
channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: U.S. Prosecutors Bring Torture Charge Against Nicolás Maduro
item.description: The deposed Venezuelan leader and his wife, already facing narcoterrorism and drug charges, are accused of conspiring to torture American detainees.

item.title: In Spain, Grief and Politics Mix After Death of Evicted Woman
item.description: The 87-year-old ‘Maricarmen’ became the face of the struggle to fix Spain’s broken housing market. Her death turned her into a political martyr.

item.title: The Far-Left Mayor on the Front Line of France’s Student Protests
item.description: Bally Bagayoko has become a hero for protesters and a lightning rod for critics who say he is sowing unrest at French schools.

item.title: Trump Says U.S. Won’t Resume Strikes on Iran Before Midterms
item.description: The president cited “productive discussions” with Tehran.

item.title: China Is Offering Half Measures to Its Mounting Economic Problems
item.description: Beijing is pursuing big technological advances while shunning painful policy measures needed to fix the broader economy.

item.title: Two Latvians Arrested After Break-In at U.K. Military Base
item.description: U.K. counterterrorism police are questioning two Latvian men after they broke into a British military base that is used as an intelligence hub by the U.S. military and NATO forces.

item.title: Russian Airstrike on Bus Stop Kills at Least 30 in Ukraine
item.description: The glide-bomb strike was the latest deadly attack in Moscow’s escalating bombardment of Ukrainian cities.

item.title: Tanker Attacks Push Deeper Into Gulf, Rattle Oil Markets
item.description: A strike near Qatar, far from the usual flashpoint at the Strait of Hormuz, raises fears of wider disruptions.

item.title: Israel Downgrades U.K. Consulate in Jerusalem Over West Bank Trade Ban
item.description: The dispute centers around the U.K.’s decision to halt trade from Israeli settlements and comes as an election looms.

item.title: Brent Gains More Than 4% on U.S.-Iran Tensions, Hurricane Isaias
item.description: Prices jumped as traders weighed intensifying Persian Gulf shipping risks and U.S.-Iran tensions alongside U.S. offshore production shut-ins ahead of Hurricane Isaias.

item.title: Canadian Poet Anne Carson Awarded Nobel Prize in Literature
item.description: The acclaimed poet, classicist and translator was lauded by the Nobel Committee for her “bold and inventive” work.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for October 2026: Up to 4.50%
item.description: These are the accounts that offer the best interest rates—without burdensome fees, gimmicks or other hassles

item.title: Oil Majors Cut Production in Gulf of Mexico as Hurricane Isaias Strengthens
item.description: Chevron, Shell and Harbour Energy have begun curbing production and evacuating personnel from offshore facilities as the region braces for the hurricane.

item.title: Texts Show Kimberly Guilfoyle Seeking $100,000 and Offering Access to Trump Officials
item.description: Plus, rogue pilots are now one of the biggest threats to airline safety—and the race is on for next summer’s $50,000 internships.

item.title: Land Mines in the Korean DMZ Deliver Warning Against Defections
item.description: Explosions in the buffer zone last month—blamed by Seoul on Pyongyang—have illustrated Kim Jong Un’s determination to keep people from fleeing south.

item.title: The Quest to Save Rural Pay Phones, 52 Calls at a Time
item.description: Driven by nostalgia—and maybe the apocalypse—an army of ‘phone spotters’ is racing against the clock to rescue the U.K.’s remote red boxes.

item.title: Spain’s Leader Pins Political Survival on Public Anger Over Housing Crisis
item.description: Pedro Sánchez is betting his left-wing coalition can avoid a bruising election defeat amid rage over the eviction of an elderly woman who died Wednesday.

item.title: Houthis Escalate Attacks on Saudi Airports, Killing 3 and Wounding Dozens
item.description: The deadly strikes deepen a conflict between the kingdom and its Iran-backed foes in Yemen.

item.title: Suspected Iranian Drone Plot in U.K. Raises Security Questions at Western Bases
item.description: The rise of drone warfare brings questions about how to protect large and expensive assets like bombers—even thousands of miles from front lines of conflict.

item.title: The Spy Crisis That Threatens to Defang Germany’s Top Intelligence Agency
item.description: The arrest of the BND’s former head complicates a planned overhaul of Berlin’s foreign intelligence service.
